cath_guide.text: Look up. That's the longest unbroken stretch of medieval Gothic vaulting in the world. About ninety-six metres of stone ribs, like the branches of an avenue of palm trees.

Where the ribs meet there are carved bosses, hundreds of them, painted: saints, beasts, even the murder of Thomas Becket. And under one of the choir seats there's a carved elephant with cow's hooves, by someone who had clearly only ever heard one described.
Halfway along the north side is the Minstrels' Gallery, with a row of carved angels playing medieval instruments: bagpipes, a harp, a citole. A heavenly folk band.
And the two great towers outside are Norman, older than all of this. The Gothic builders kept them and built round them. Waste not, want not.

cath_clock.text: The astronomical clock, from the 1400s. The Earth in the middle, the sun and moon going round it, which was the latest science at the time.
See the little round hole in the door below it? The story is it was cut for the bishop's cat, to get in and catch the mice that came after the grease on the clockwork.
Some say that's where 'Hickory dickory dock' comes from. The mouse ran up the clock. I say it's a very good story and you should buy a postcard.

exe_ringer.text: Six bells up the stairs, a rope each, and a band who've been ringing together longer than most marriages last. We need a hand. The treble, the tenor, whichever one's gone for a tea.
